messages.text: Good question to start with! It really comes down to the space: a floor globe (usually 40-50 inches tall on its own stand) makes a real statement in a study or living room, while a desktop globe sits neatly on a desk, shelf, or credenza. Which space did you have in mind for it?
I am looking for a large globe for my husband with some visual impairment

That's thoughtful of you. For visual impairment, I'd suggest the Statesman 20-inch Illuminated Blue Ocean Floor Globe with Walnut Stand. The blue ocean map gives strong, bright contrast between water and land so labels and coastlines are easier to pick out, the raised relief lets him feel mountain ranges and borders with his fingers, and the illumination adds extra light to read by in the evening. At 20 inches it's also one of our largest, so details are bigger and easier to see. Shipping is free on that one.

Here's more on why blue ocean reads more easily: [Blue Ocean or Antique: Which Globe Is Easier to Read?](https://replogleglobes.ca/blogs/the-globe-guide/blue-ocean-vs-antique-globe-readability)

You'll find it under "Statesman 20-inch Illuminated Blue Ocean Floor Globe with Walnut Stand" in the search bar, ready to add to your cart.
